name: Soldering Iron

claims.claim_text: Two constructions dominate. In the older one the tip slides over a separate heating element with the temperature sensor buried somewhere in that assembly, the exact arrangement varying by manufacturer.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's where the thermocouple lives
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: In the newer one the element and the sensor are built into the tip itself, so replacing the tip replaces the heater and the sensor with it, and the feedback path no longer runs through a mechanical contact or an air gap.
claims.quote_verbatim: the temperature sensor is all integrated into the tip
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Telling them apart takes no disassembly: an old-technology tip is a bare piece of formed metal with no electrical contacts on it.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's just the tip itself
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The property that actually matters in use is recovery. Each joint pulls heat out of the tip and drops its temperature, and the time taken to climb back is what limits working through a row of joints.
claims.quote_verbatim: your soldering iron dips in temperature
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: That recovery time is not simply a matter of wattage. Peak power, the drive circuitry, the temperature sensor's own thermal response and the physical design of the tip all sit inside the same control loop.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's also related to your temperature sensor and how quick a thermal response based on the design of the tip
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Integrated-tip designs win on that measure because the element, the heater and the tip were engineered as one object, so the loop sees the disturbance sooner and applies power sooner.
claims.quote_verbatim: the element the heater and the tip are all in the one purpose design physical thing
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The clearest illustration of thermal mass is at the other end of the trade: irons sold for copper plumbing run at a hundred and fifty watts with an enormous tip, purely because the work keeps taking heat away.
claims.quote_verbatim: it needs so much heat capacity just to keep dumping heat into the into the copper
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Cartridge irons work by induction rather than a resistive element, and they detect the cradle so the iron shuts down when set down and is hot again by the time it reaches the work.
claims.quote_verbatim: when it's in the cradle, it shuts itself off
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Buying tips for such a system means choosing a shape and a temperature band together, since the temperature is a property of the cartridge rather than of the station.
claims.quote_verbatim: you buy basically a temperature range instead
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: That is the real cost of the architecture: with no controller in the station, covering several tip shapes across several temperatures means keeping an array of perhaps twenty cartridges at ten to fifteen dollars each.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got to have an array of like 20 tips
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Tip design itself is a deliberate compromise between working life and thermal performance, set by the cladding material and the thermal resistance it adds — a long-life tip and a very low-resistance tip are not the same tip.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't have a long life tip and a really super low resistance, efficient tip
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The two axes are independent, and expensive irons do not all sit on the same one: a high-end station may still be dial-controlled with a direct-heat tip rather than using temperature-selecting cartridges.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can dial in the temperature, but it uses a direct heat tip
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Old tip-over-element irons remain perfectly good for low thermal mass work; it is high-mass joints that expose the difference and justify keeping a separate iron for them.
claims.quote_verbatim: They work good for low mass stuff
claims.speaker: David Ray
claims.episode_title: Electronics Manufacturing History with David Ray

claims.claim_text: The temperature an iron is set to is far above the melting point of the alloy, and the discrepancy against a datasheet's stated maximum confuses people reasonably often.
claims.quote_verbatim: my soldering iron is 800 degrees
claims.speaker: Scott Driscoll
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: The explanation is that the profiles in a datasheet describe mass reflow of the whole assembly, not a hand tool, and a hand tool has to overcome the heat running away from the part into the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: which have to compensate for all the heat running away from the part
claims.speaker: Scott Driscoll
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: A common working setting on a fixed-temperature cartridge is around three hundred and seventy degrees Celsius, which is high but conventional for this reason.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's 370 degrees Celsius.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Tip selection matters more than the user interface, which on most stations amounts to setting a temperature once and leaving it.
claims.quote_verbatim: I just set a temperature and I keep it there
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: The useful tips are the ones that serve two purposes at once — a large body carrying thermal mass that still ends in a fine point, or a knife shape usable on its edge for detail and on its full blade for bulk.
claims.quote_verbatim: I like the knife tips
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: The conical tip that irons ship with by default is the least useful of the common shapes.
claims.quote_verbatim: So I don't like conical tips.
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: Very fine work may need a separate smaller handpiece rather than just a smaller tip, since the handle itself determines what tips will fit.
claims.quote_verbatim: I got an extra smaller
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Two irons is not indulgence but technique: with one on each end of a small part you can lift it straight off the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: you got to have two soldering irons so that you can flip parts off
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The point is common enough among people who do this daily to be stated flatly as equipment advice.
claims.quote_verbatim: Need two soldier and irons, by the way.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Removing parts from old boards is a separate thermal problem again, and generally calls for a high-power iron.
claims.quote_verbatim: Get your 100 watt iron out
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Armstrong, Camenzind & Museums - Outstanding Oneirophoros Obituaries

claims.claim_text: The practical threshold is lower than enthusiasm suggests: any temperature-controlled iron will do the job.
claims.quote_verbatim: anything temperature control is going to work
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The genuine failure case is an abused tool rather than a cheap one — an iron that has been run all day at an event until it barely melts solder is a different proposition.
claims.quote_verbatim: it barely melts solder anymore
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: It is also worth resisting the inference that good work comes from a good iron; the honest claim is only that the tool is not a bad one.
claims.quote_verbatim: not that it's such a good iron. I'm saying that it's not a terrible iron
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: At the low end, an inexpensive pencil taking a widely-copied cartridge standard costs about thirty dollars and handles lead-free work without complaint.
claims.quote_verbatim: Quico is a brand I found on Ali express for about 30 bucks
claims.speaker: Greg Davill

claims.claim_text: Portable irons powered over a USB connection now exist in the same price range with reasonable build quality.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's like 30 bucks.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The limitation of running an iron from a small portable source is thermal capacity rather than temperature — an unregulated mains pencil or a gas iron at least has some heat behind it.
claims.quote_verbatim: they got some bloody thermal capacity
claims.episode_title: Hyperloop, Upverter and Soldering - Unbelievable USB Ustulater

claims.claim_text: Between the mid-range and the top of the market the price gap is large, and the question worth asking is not which is best but how long the tool is expected to last.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want it to be a 10-year soldering iron or a 5-year soldering iron or a 2-week soldering iron
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Irons priced around a thousand dollars are aimed at production work — instant heat and tightly held temperature — rather than at anyone working occasionally.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not for a hobbyist to be buying
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The value position sits in between, where clones of the premium induction systems deliver most of the behaviour for a fraction of the price.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a Metcal clone
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Upgrading from genuinely poor equipment is noticeable in the work itself, which is the honest argument for spending more: bad joints and frustration trace back to the tool.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was starting to affect some of my, my solder joints
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: There is a defensible argument for preferring a copy of a current-technology iron over a genuine example of the older technology at the same price, if the newer heating architecture is what you are buying.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can buy a rip-off of the new technology for the same price as a genuine old technology one
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The market has moved from analogue dials to digital controls with preset temperatures, which is a real loss for anyone who wants to grab a knob and see the setting.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're going to stop selling the analog model
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Processors, CEOs & Soldering irons - Plentiful Perfunctory Programs

claims.claim_text: Some now take firmware updates, which is a genuinely new category of thing to go wrong in a hand tool.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's a lot of USB connected soldering irons
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Don't Turn It On, Don't Take It Apart

claims.claim_text: Almost all of them use a fixed transformer and cannot be switched between mains voltages, which is the trap when buying equipment from another region.
claims.quote_verbatim: They're fixed transformer, almost all of them.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The internals are simple enough to recombine: a genuine handpiece, an aftermarket controller board and a cordless drill battery make a working portable station in a day.
claims.quote_verbatim: he hacked together a Heiko, a portable Heiko, genuine Heiko soldering iron using a drill battery pack
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Road trip to the deep space network

claims.claim_text: An oversized part on small pads is soldered without the tip ever touching the pad — the lead is heated and conducts into the joint underneath.
claims.quote_verbatim: you put the soldering iron on the lead and then that heats up the pad
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The reason to buy an optical microscope rather than a cheap camera one is working distance: the height above the board is what leaves room to get an iron underneath.
claims.quote_verbatim: being able to get a soldering iron underneath it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Beginners commonly try to do everything at once — holding the part, the board, the iron and the solder — when the answer is to set the work up first and understand that the joint needs a moment to take heat.
claims.quote_verbatim: they try and hold the component and hold the PCB
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Teaching it can be almost entirely hands-off: cover the safety points, demonstrate once, and let the learner do it rather than delivering half an hour of instruction first.
claims.quote_verbatim: This is the hot end. This is the not hot end.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Over a couple of days a group with no engineering background can be taken from not recognising the hardware to soldering on it, probing it and reverse engineering the board.
claims.quote_verbatim: have a soldering iron to it and a logic analyzer to it
claims.speaker: Joe Grand
claims.episode_title: New Life Skills with Joe Grand
